_readme: Shared defaults. Per-project overrides go in <project>/.claude/hooks.config.json (see README.md, Project-local overrides).

arch_rules._comment: Block file writes that violate package boundary rules. Set enabled=true and define rules.

content_watch._comment: Run a validation command whenever a matching file is written. Leave validate_command empty to disable.

bash_description_guard._comment: Block (exit 2) any Bash call that lacks a non-empty `description` field. Enforces terminal command discipline: explain WHY and WHAT before running.

env_guard._comment: Block (exit 2) Read calls targeting .env or .env.* files. Environment files contain secrets and must not be read by the assistant. NOTE: check-env-guard.js does not read this config; the block is unconditional and `enabled` currently has no effect.

push_audit._comment: Before any git push, audits staged (or HEAD~1, or the empty tree for a root commit) diff for: hardcoded secrets (BLOCK), debug statements, commented-out code, missing tests, lockfile drift. Reports PASS/BLOCK with per-finding severity.

_checks.secrets: HIGH — blocks push. Detects API keys, passwords, tokens, private keys in added lines.
_checks.debug_statements: MEDIUM — console.log, debugger, pprint in non-test files.
_checks.commented_code: LOW — 3+ commented-out code lines added in a single file.
_checks.lockfile_drift: MEDIUM — package.json changed without a lockfile update.
_checks.missing_tests: MEDIUM — source files changed with zero test file changes.

branch_delete_guard._comment: Blocks `git push <remote> --delete <branch>` (and the `:branch` shorthand) when an open GitHub PR still has that branch as its base. Deleting a stacked PR's base branch does not merge it — GitHub auto-closes it instead (its commits usually aren't in the new target yet), and a closed PR's base can't be retargeted; the only recovery is opening a brand-new PR from the same branch/commits. Requires the gh CLI, authenticated — fails open (allows, with a warning) if gh is unavailable, so a stale check never blocks otherwise-normal work. Local `git branch -D` is intentionally out of scope, since that alone can't break a GitHub PR's base.

ci_status_check._comment: After any git push, blocks (synchronously) until the matching GitHub Actions run for that exact commit completes, and reports the real pass/fail result. Requires the gh CLI, authenticated. Adds real wall-clock wait time to every push — roughly however long your CI takes to run. If your repo has no GitHub Actions workflow, this harmlessly reports 'no run found' once per push (new_run_timeout_seconds) and exits 1 informationally.
ci_status_check._new_run_timeout_note: How long to wait for a run matching the just-pushed commit SHA to even appear in `gh run list`.
ci_status_check._completion_timeout_note: Currently unenforced — check-ci-status-after-push.js uses `gh run watch` for this phase, which blocks until the run finishes with no timeout flag of its own. Left here as a documented intent for a future implementer, not a working setting.

merge_guard._comment: Unconditionally blocks `gh pr merge`, a PUT to the `gh api .../pulls/{n}/merge` REST equivalent, a local `git merge` on master/main, and any push (refspec or plain branch name) that lands commits directly on master/main. A hook can't verify from inside a Bash call whether a human already gave permission in conversation, so instead of trying it blocks every matching command, every time — the merge has to happen on the actual GitHub PR page after a human explicitly says go-ahead.

search_guard._comment: Nudge (or block) raw shell search/read commands (grep, find, cat, head, tail, ...) in favor of the assistant's own dedicated search/read tools, which return structured, token-bounded results instead of raw stdout dumps.
search_guard._on_violation_note: 'warn' prints to stderr (exit 0) | 'block' exits 2 and rejects the tool call
search_guard._allow_patterns_note: Substrings that, if present anywhere in the command, skip the check entirely — e.g. a known-legitimate build/CI command that happens to invoke grep/cat internally.

dep_guard._comment: Warn (non-blocking) when Claude runs a command that adds a dependency. Extend warn_patterns for your ecosystem.

empty_test_guard._comment: Fail (exit 1) when a test file is written with empty test suites or empty test bodies. Prevents theater testing.
empty_test_guard._test_file_patterns_note: Glob-style patterns. Files matching any of these are inspected.
empty_test_guard._block_todo_tests_note: If true, fail on it.todo() / test.todo() blocks (useful in strict mode)

todo_format._comment: Warn when TODO comments do not follow the required format. Set enabled=true to activate.
todo_format._required_pattern_note: Regex. Default enforces 'TODO(owner): description'. Set to null to only warn on bare TODO without any format.

script_guard._comment: Warn before running 'npm run X' / 'pnpm run X' etc. when the script does not exist in package.json. Prevents silent no-ops.
script_guard._package_json_paths_note: List of package.json files to check for script existence. Extend for monorepos.
script_guard._on_missing_note: 'warn' prints to stderr (exit 0) | 'block' exits 1 and prevents the command

commit_guard._comment: Warn or block git commit commands that do not include WHY and EXPECTED sections in the message.
commit_guard._on_violation_note: warn prints to stderr (exit 0) | block exits 2 and rejects the tool call

commands._comment: Reference commands for documentation and session-start banner. These are NOT auto-run — use content_watch.validate_command for automated execution.
